title: CBSE 2027 board exams: UAE schools intensify revision and mock tests as students and parents raise concerns over tight schedules and limited revision time - Education Times

 News › News News › CBSE 2027 board exams: UAE schools intensify revision and mock tests as students and parents raise c… CBSE 2027 board exams: UAE schools intensify revision and mock tests as students and parents raise concerns over tight schedules and limited revision time
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 08:41 IST CBSE 2027 board exams: UAE schools hasten preparations Schools across the United Arab Emirates have entered a decisive preparation phase for the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations. Fewer than 100 days remain before the first paper.
 Institutions are expanding revision sessions, scheduling mock examinations and offering additional academic support, even as some students and parents voice unease about the structure of the examination timetable.
 The 2027 board examinations will begin on February 16. Class 10 papers will conclude on March 9, while Class 12 examinations will continue until April 9. The board released the date sheet on November 6. 
 This gave schools a limited window to complete their syllabuses and move into intensive revision.
 Early syllabus completion and mock examinations 
 Delhi Private School (DPS) Dubai expects to finish its syllabus by the end of November. The school will then hold two rounds of mock examinations, one in December and one in January. According to Rashmi Nandkeolyar, the school's principal and director, these assessments allow students to practise under examination conditions and identify the topics that need more attention.
 She noted that preparation for board examinations begins well before students reach the final two years of school. The school focuses on conceptual understanding and its practical application. It believes this approach benefits students in both board examinations and international benchmarking assessments.
 DPS Dubai also runs remedial classes for students who need extra help, alongside enrichment programmes for those seeking greater academic challenge. 
 Nandkeolyar acknowledged that the schedule is somewhat tighter this year. She said the school intends to provide as much practice as possible within the available time, so students enter the examination hall confident and well prepared.
 Concerns over consecutive papers 
 The most prominent concern among families relates to the spacing of certain papers. At Woodlem Park School in Ajman, students and parents have pointed to short gaps between some subjects, particularly where papers fall on consecutive days. 
 Principal Bhanu Sharma said families believe longer intervals would allow more effective revision and help students manage stress.
 Sharma explained that schools must work within the timetable set by the board. They cannot alter the dates themselves. Instead, institutions are responding with structured revision plans, additional academic guidance and counselling services. These measures aim to help students plan their study time carefully and remain composed during the examination period.
 Lingering questions over evaluation 
 The preparations follow a year in which the board's evaluation process came under scrutiny. The introduction of on-screen marking for Class 12 answer sheets in 2026 attracted criticism. Allegations included technical difficulties, marking inaccuracies and discrepancies in marks awarded. These raised questions about the accuracy and transparency of the process. The reported problems, however, do not establish that all results were affected.
 Experiences among UAE schools appear to vary. Deepika Thapar Singh, CEO and principal of Credence High School, said no parents at her school had raised concerns about corrections or marking. She added that her school sees no significant difficulty in preparing its Class 10 and 12 students.
 Emphasis on a calm approach 
 Singh argued that schools should avoid creating undue anxiety around board examinations. In her view, a well-planned calendar, regular classes, consistent attendance and diligent completion of assignments largely take care of preparation. 
 She said her school prefers a calm and reassuring atmosphere to one of panic. This allows students to perform as they would in any other assessment.
 With the examination window approaching, UAE schools are balancing academic rigour with student wellbeing. Early syllabus completion, repeated mock assessments, targeted remedial support and counselling form the core of their strategies. While the concerns over closely spaced papers are unlikely to be resolved at school level, institutions appear committed to helping students make the best use of the time available. For families, the coming weeks will depend on disciplined revision, steady communication with teachers and a measured approach to the pressures of the board examination season.
